claims.statement: Regional Terraform restricts deployments to the configured account, requires at least two task subnets with default outbound routes, and constrains Bedrock endpoint subnets to the task VPC with one subnet per availability zone.
The Fargate task definition mounts an EFS-backed home with empty task-scoped OCM and kubeconfig overlays, and when enabled makes the main container depend on a healthy kube-proxy sidecar.
Regional EFS is encrypted, provides an access point as UID/GID 1000, and its filesystem policy's EnforceAccessViaAccessPoint statement requires the task role to mount through an access point.

The investigation audit bucket is versioned, uses compliance-mode Object Lock, blocks public access, applies AES-256 server-side encryption, and denies non-TLS requests; cross-account replication is optional.

The create-investigation Lambda supports ZIP and container-image modes with shared environment configuration; image mode derives an ordinary ECR URI from account, Region and project and requires a lowercase 40-character SHA tag. EventBridge separately invokes the task reaper on a schedule.

Account Terraform owns explicit Bedrock model offer agreements; regional Terraform validates that the default inference profile maps to an approved foundation model and tests reject bare model IDs and unapproved mappings.
Bedrock Runtime access is routed through a private interface endpoint, while invocation text logging uses encrypted CloudWatch Logs and sends large payloads to a separate S3 bucket.

The EFS filesystem policy's AllowReaperViaDedicatedAccessPoint statement grants the reap-investigations Lambda role ClientMount/ClientWrite/ClientRootAccess scoped by elasticfilesystem:AccessPointArn to a single dedicated access point (aws_efs_access_point.reaper, UID/GID 0, rooted at '/'), kept separate from the task role's access-point-scoped grant and deliberately not extended to dynamically created per-investigation access points.

The investigation reaper's DeleteAccessPoint grant targets access-point ARNs in the current account and Region and requires aws:ResourceTag/ManagedBy=rosa-boundary-lambda; this is separate from the filesystem grant that requires the dedicated reaper access point for mounting.

The investigation reaper uses an account-owned IAM role with basic and VPC execution managed-policy attachments, while regional Terraform owns its log group and inline ECS/EFS/S3 grants. ECS list/describe is cluster-conditioned, task-definition list/deregister uses wildcard resources, access-point deletion requires the ManagedBy tag on current-region/account access-point ARNs, and filesystem mount/write/root access requires the dedicated reaper access point.

The investigation reaper mounts its dedicated EFS root access point at /mnt/efs and runs on an independent EventBridge schedule set by the investigation_reaper_schedule_hours Terraform variable (default 8 hours). With no matching running task, creation age beyond the grace period (investigation_grace_period_hours, default 168 hours) or missing CreatedAt makes an investigation eligible; a final task check precedes cleanup, and an existing directory requires a successful S3 backup under cluster/investigation/reaper-final-backup before directory deletion, access-point removal, and task-definition deregistration.

Account state owns shared IAM role identities, trusts and common managed-policy attachments; the regional root looks up these roles and owns regional inline grants. The legacy-policy Region has unsuffixed inline-policy names; other Regions append a Region suffix, so shared roles receive the union of scoped regional grants.

The account-owned Bedrock logging role retains SourceAccount restriction and permits only configured regional SourceArn patterns; an empty account region list falls back to the legacy role-tag region. Staging explicitly approves east and west, while regional roots retain their own logging destinations and delivery grants.

Every regional deployment unconditionally creates a published-content S3 bucket (<account>-<project>-<stage>-<region>-content), kept separate from the write-once audit bucket; it has versioning but no Object Lock, a lifecycle rule that only expires noncurrent versions and aborted multipart uploads (current objects are never expired), full public-access blocking, and a bucket policy denying non-TLS requests, non-aws:kms uploads, uploads naming a foreign KMS key, and any SSE-C upload.

The content bucket encrypts with the Region's AWS-managed alias/aws/s3 key rather than a customer-managed key; deploy/regional creates no KMS key. A reserved _bootstrap/key-init object, written with an explicit aws:kms request, guarantees the key exists, after which data.aws_kms_alias.content_s3 resolves its real ARN for every subsequent grant and policy statement. S3 Bucket Keys are deliberately left disabled because enabling them would move the KMS encryption context to the bucket ARN and require kms:Decrypt in the AWS-managed key's policy, which this design cannot edit.

content_prefixes is the single source of truth for publisher grants and the runtime subdirectory layout; Terraform validation requires its values to be distinct, non-overlapping, directory-style (/-terminated) paths, and rejects any prefix that is an ancestor of the reserved _bootstrap/ key.

deploy/regional/iam-content.tf defines an unconditional task content-read grant scoped to the content bucket, separately gated per-prefix publisher grants using a dedicated role and a replication grant enabled by destination configuration; publisher policy omits GetObject and wildcard permissions, while replication uses a different identity from audit replication.

Content replication reuses the generic replication topology object shared with deploy/account; only replication.primary_region activates source-side content rules and grants (publisher grants are preconditioned to the same region), aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration.content renders one rule per (destination, prefix) pair with a prefix-count priority stride, and lifecycle preconditions reject a destination bucket name outside the shared naming convention, a replica KMS key outside the destination region, a content_prefixes mismatch with the source map, or a destination equal to the workspace's own region; destination metadata must arrive as plain input values rather than terraform_remote_state.

The account root's shared-iam module owns the content publisher and content-replication IAM role identities (exposed via content_publisher_role_arns and content_replication_role_arn outputs); deploy/regional resolves each role by name from its supplied ARN and owns every inline grant on it, following the same account/regional ownership split and regional_policy_suffix naming used for the other shared roles.
